Hexalobular Drive — Also Known as Torx

A Six-Pointed Star Pattern

The hexalobular drive is a screwdriver recess with a 6-pointed, star-shaped pattern. It is the drive type called out by the “T” characters in the part number.

Higher Torque Transfer

Driving forces are carried through surfaces rather than edges, so there is less wear on the tool and no damage to the surface treatment.

Longer Tool Life & No Slipping

Optimal torque transmission extends the working life of driving tools and prevents the “cam-out” slipping typical of cross-recess drives.

The six-lobed Torx recess on the Item H1 screw heads.

Ideal for industrial and consumer applications that need precision and durability — and the small head needs less clearance while still absorbing the load.

Topic T4 · Material Selection

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

The “S” in .6C30TTCS/PR calls out the base material. The extended description (“S/S”) and the item specification both confirm it: stainless steel, grade 18-8.

Requirement

Material: stainless steel · Grade: 18-8 (A2) stainless steel, as listed in the Item Specifications.

What “18-8” Means

18-8 is an American term for a common grade of stainless steel containing 18% chromium and 8% nickel.

Equivalent Grade

Equivalent to type 304 stainless steel (the “A2” family).

Corrosion Resistance

Good corrosion resistance in typical service environments.

Strength

Medium strength — lower than alloy steel grades, which is the usual trade-off for corrosion resistance.

Why It Matters

18-8 is the default stainless callout across most of SBS's fastener line, which keeps sourcing and lead times predictable.

Quick Reference: The Decoded Part Number

Keep this in mind — the same breakdown from Topic T2, all in one place.

.6C30TTCS/PR
  • .Metric. The leading period marks this as a metric fastener.
  • 6Diameter. An M6 nominal diameter (6 mm, 1.0 mm pitch).
  • CCoarse Thread. A coarse thread pitch, not fine.
  • 30Length. 30 mm overall.
  • TDrive Type. A Torx (hexalobular) drive.
  • TTorx Type. The T30 six-lobe drive — needs a T30 Torx driver.
  • CCone Head. A conical head shape.
  • SMaterial. 18-8 (A2) stainless steel.
  • /PRPer Print. Made to the customer print.

Reference

Glossary

Every code, acronym, and term used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term's “jump” button to see it in context.

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

A common grade of stainless steel, roughly equivalent to type 304. “18-8” is the American term for stainless steel with 18% chromium and 8% nickel. It's the default stainless callout across most of SBS's fastener line.

BRP

Bombardier Recreational Products — one of SBS's customers, and the owner of the print for this part. About 750 pieces of Item H1 ship to BRP every two to three days.

Cone Head

A conical, low-profile screw head shape, called out by the second “C” in the part number.

E-Coat Black

The coating process run on this part under transaction 87709, turning .6C30TTCS/PR into .6C30TTCS/PRMET. It was required by the customer.

Hexalobular Drive (Torx)

A drive recess with a six-pointed, star-shaped pattern. It gives higher torque transfer, reduced tool wear and no cam-out slipping. This part uses size T30, so it needs a T30 driver. “6-Lobe” is another name for it.

Item Master Inquiry

The P21 screen that shows an item's criteria, inventory, sales history, process history and more, by company and location.

Per Print (PR)

The “/PR” suffix: the part is made to the customer's controlled print rather than to a general standard.

POD

SBS's system of controlled customer prints. Check it for further details when the print isn't visible in P21.

PPAP

Production Part Approval Process — the documentation package a supplier submits to prove its process can reliably make a part to print before full production begins. This part is PPAP Level 3 (Class 5).

PROP 65

A California law requiring a warning label on products containing certain chemicals above a set threshold. “Compliant” here means the part doesn't trigger that warning.

REACH

A European Union regulation restricting hazardous chemicals in manufactured goods — a separate compliance check from RoHS, covering a broader list of substances.

RoHS

Restriction of Hazardous Substances — an EU rule limiting materials like lead and mercury in manufactured parts.
